messages:
lina: seeing a spike of mTLS handshake failures from apac ingress after yesterday's keystore perms change. error from the edge logs: "tls: handshake failure: remote error: handshake failure". anyone else seeing this? :rotating_light:

ajay: yep noticed increased 502s, mostly between edge-proxy-apac -> internal-ingress. Happened ~09:12 UTC after deploy. Rolling back RBAC is an option but want a quicker triage first.

maya: can you paste the exact error lines? also which keystore change was applied? was it the new bind-mount ACLs to /etc/redwood/keystore?

lina: logs snippet: ```
Apr 12 09:12:41 edge-proxy-apac nginx[2145]: 2026/04/12 09:12:41 [error] 2145#0: *12345 upstream SSL handshake failed (SSL: error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure) while SSL handshaking to upstream, client: 10.12.1.5, server: ingress, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1"
```
keystore change: applied RBAC policy that removed read access to keystore for service-account `internal-ingress` and added conditional KMS decrypt via new role.

dena: :eyes: that RBAC prune could explain it if the proxy can no longer access the private key to complete the handshake. but mTLS means both client and server certs matter. can we confirm whether the keystore file exists with correct mode on the pod? quick check: `kubectl exec -n infra internal-ingress-xxx -- ls -la /etc/redwood/keystore`

ajay: I ran `kubectl exec` and got permission denied even as infra-admin. the service account token used by the pod can't read the mount now. however KMS decrypt logs show a successful UnwrapKey call around the same time. kms-bot: event id `kms-ev-98765` (successful UnwrapKey for key `projects/redwood/keys/edge-priv-rot-v2`)

kms-bot: KMS audit: "principal:system:serviceaccount:infra:internal-ingress" UnwrapKey SUCCESS 2026-04-12T09:12:40Z id=kms-ev-98765

maya: interesting — KMS unwrap ok but file-level read blocked. Two possibilities: (1) keystore material is being retrieved successfully but then written to a path with restrictive ACLs (umask or chown issue), (2) the TLS library tries to access the key directly from filesystem and RBAC prevents the container from opening it.

lina: repro attempt on a staging pod: `kubectl cp` of keystore to local showed file present, owner root:root, mode 0400. internal-ingress container runs as `redwood-internal` uid 1500. previously the init-container changed ownership to that user. I suspect the init step failed after RBAC change.

ajay: can we check audit logs for the init-container that writes keystore? `kubectl logs -n infra init-keystore-xxx` — maybe it couldn't chown because it couldn't access KMS credentials.

dena: I pulled logs: init container shows `permission denied` when attempting `chown 1500:1500 /etc/redwood/keystore` and then continues without failing (bug). So runtime proceeds but file stays 0400 root.

maya: aha. that's the root cause. fix strategy: (a) immediate hotfix: patch init container to explicitly fail on chown error so we don't start with bad perms, (b) short-term rollback: reapply previous RBAC that allowed init to mutate the mount, (c) medium-term: move keystore handling to a sidecar that mounts emptyDir and retains proper ownership via an init job with correct podSecurityContext.

lina: can someone own the rollback to restore service ASAP? we should also rotate any keys if they were touched suspiciously.

ajay: I'll do a scoped rollback for infra namespace to last known-good RBAC policy (ID: rbac-policy-2026-04-11). rolling back now. posting deploy bot info...

security-bot: alert created: S-2026-042-KMS-KESTORE. Severity: medium. Actions recommended: rotate keys if private key material was exfiltrated, preserve audit logs, run quick sig-checks on cert chain.

maya: before rotating keys, verify if any external unusual access happened. KMS audit shows only UnwrapKey from internal-ingress service account at 09:12. no external principals. also no large exports in blobstore logs. I think rotate is precautionary but not evidence-based.

dena: rollback completed at 09:24 UTC; 502 rate back down to baseline in 90s. i'll run a small smoke test and confirm mTLS handshakes succeed.

lina: smoke looks good. we still need the follow-ups: 1) make init container fail on chown error (PR), 2) add an automated test that simulates restricted file perms and fails CI if handshake breaks, 3) add audit alert for InitContainer chown errors.

ajay: I'll open the PR for init behavior and push a canary to staging. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/init-keystore-fail-on-chown

maya: for the audit side: query that helped triage: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=k8s_container AND protoPayload.methodName=\"io.k8s.kubernetes.pkg.apis.authorization.v1.SubjectAccessReview\" AND textPayload:\"chown\"" --limit 50` — adds a filter for attempted chown failures in init logs.

lina: also adding per-region fallback policy: if keystore unavailable, fallback to a cached ephemeral cert for 10m and alert. we'll coordinate with product.

security-bot: added follow-up ticket S-2026-042-FU: require init container non-zero exit on keystore setup fail; assign to ajay, severity high for infra init fix.

dena: thumbs up. one more ops note — we should validate TLS cipher configuration after any keystore rotation. sample check: `openssl s_client -connect ingress.apac.redwood.ai:443 -tls1_3 -ciphersuites TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 -showcerts` and also check mTLS client cert verification path.

maya: agreed. i'll add an automatic nightly scan that runs `openssl s_client` + parse handshake for each edge region and posts results to #eng-sre.

lina: thanks all. closing thread after PR merges and audit ticket updated. :white_check_mark:
